cards.q: Paddy Galloway's 3 intro rules?
cards.a2:
1. Confirm the click.
2. Contradiction / hook.
3. A seamless bridge into the content.

cards.q: Bad bridge vs good bridge: give an example of each.
cards.a2:
Bad: "I'll show you 3 methods. Now let's get into it."
Good: "I'll show you 3 methods, and the first one is to…"

cards.q: Paddy's minute-3 test?
cards.a2: Stop a viewer at 3:00. He should be able to say "he'll explain Y, at the end he shows X, and he mentioned Z so I want that too." If he says "no idea where it's going", there's no curiosity.

cards.q: Where did viewers leave your first 3 videos, and what does that mean for every intro?
cards.a2: Between 0:22 and 0:37. So a loop has to be open by about 0:30.

cards.q: On face channels, which kind of opening wins and which loses?
cards.a2:
Result-first: 15% of winners vs 5% of medians.
Greeting / intro first: 9% of winners vs 22% of medians.

cards.q: Why show, not just say, in the first 5 seconds?
cards.a2: Autoplay previews are muted. The picture has to sell the click.

cards.q: Entertainment intro vs educational intro: what is each one's job?
cards.a2:
Entertainment: prove you'll actually do what the thumbnail says.
Educational: show why YOU are worth listening to (perceived effort, credibility).

cards.q: After the click is confirmed, which 3 things should the rest of the intro do?
cards.a2: Open a new curiosity gap, give context, and show perceived effort.

cards.q: Aprilynne's "most important step" trick?
cards.a2: Frame step 1 as the most important, even if it's a prerequisite (packaging, "be lean first"). Then frame each next step as crucial in a new way. The biggest drop is at the start, so that's where the hook goes.

cards.q: What does a 10-second self-test do in an intro? Give an example.
cards.a2:
It's a replay magnet: people rewatch it.
Example: "Check your face tonight vs tomorrow morning. If it's slimmer at night, that's water, not fat."

cards.q: Two speech openers from Talk Like TED?
cards.a2: A question that matters to the viewer (his problem, framed as a question), or a surprising stat that reframes the topic.

cards.q: How much of your scripting time should go to the intro?
cards.a2: About half (Ali Abdaal). Realistically about a third for you.

cards.q: When should your personality show, and what's the risk?
cards.a2: In the first 15 seconds, so the viewer knows who he's spending the next 15 minutes with. The risk: if it looks like just joking around, it reads as low value. Show you know your stuff too.

cards.q: Opening that worked for many of your notes' creators: the obsession intro?
cards.a2: Say you've been obsessed with the topic and studied it for a long time (SHOW it), then reveal it's actually a simple N-step formula you'll walk through.

cards.q: Made to Stick's 6 principles (SUCCESs)?
cards.a2: Simple, Unexpected, Concrete, Credible, Emotional, Stories.

cards.q: The tappers experiment: numbers and lesson?
cards.a2:
120 songs tapped, listeners guessed 3 (2.5%). Tappers predicted 50%.
Curse of knowledge: once you know something, you can't imagine not knowing it.

cards.q: Viewer intelligence vs viewer knowledge: the rule?
cards.a2: Never underestimate his intelligence. Never overestimate his prior knowledge.

cards.q: What does the movie-popcorn example teach?
cards.a2: Package a stat concretely. Not "37 g of saturated fat" but "more than bacon & eggs, a Big Mac and fries, and a steak dinner, combined". It made people stop buying it.

cards.q: The 5 small emotional moments to drop every few seconds?
cards.a2: Curiosity ("there's one exception…"), surprise ("I expected this to work, it didn't"), humour, suspense ("we'll come back to this"), relief ("the good news is…").

cards.q: Your blue/red pattern-interrupt idea?
cards.a2: Build the expectation that blue wins, then say red. Viewers who were coasting snap back to full attention, and they remember the moment.

cards.q: Oscar Patel's mid-video rehook: what did he do?
cards.a2: When it got slow: higher energy, "I know you're getting bored, lock in", reminded them why it matters for their life, and begged them to ACT, not just keep watching.

cards.q: What went wrong in the Hormozi presentation you watched?
cards.a2: No signposting. You didn't know step 1 had ended, so starting step 3 gave no dopamine. Always mark where the viewer is.

cards.q: A plot vs B plot?
cards.a2:
A plot: what the packaging promises.
B plot: something extra the viewer didn't expect. It's the opposite of clickbait and builds trust.

cards.q: MrBeast's advice to Fabio Morena?
cards.a2: Underpromise, overdeliver. Packaging as strong as possible, but the video gives way more. That's how viewers become fans.

cards.q: Aristotle's 3 parts of persuasion?
cards.a2:
Ethos: credibility. Logos: logic and data. Pathos: emotion.
Logic alone doesn't persuade.

cards.q: What does every story need, and who plays which part on your channel?
cards.a2:
A hero to root for, a villain, and a turn.
Hero: your method or the viewer. Villain: blackpill, myths, salt, the "designed to fail" system. Townspeople: your audience.
cards.src: Talk Like TED / Winning the Story Wars

cards.q: 5 ways to create a jaw-dropping moment?
cards.a2: Props and demos, shocking stats, pictures and video, a memorable repeatable line, a personal story.

cards.q: Which humour works best in a video?
cards.a2: Small observations and self-deprecation, not jokes about competitors. It should amplify the point, not distract. Don't repeat the same joke.

cards.q: Intro Lab: concrete steps vs vague, escalating vs flat?
cards.a2:
Concrete steps: 77% of hits vs 33%.
Escalating structure: 85% vs 36%.

cards.q: How should a video end?
cards.a2: On value (87% of hits vs 28%): the best result or tip, a one-line recap, then a CTA that flows into the next video.

cards.q: "If the viewer would imagine it…"
cards.a2: …draw it or show it, so his brain can focus on what you're saying instead of imagining.

cards.q: The distracted-viewer test?
cards.a2: Watch the video like a viewer with a phone next to you. Where you reach for the phone, it's boring: fix that part. Better: get someone else to do it before they've heard about the video.

cards.q: Einstein's simplicity line, and why creators break it?
cards.a2: "If you can't explain it simply, you don't understand it well enough." Creators over-explain to show how much they know. The job is to inform the viewer, not impress him.

cards.q: Bite-sized chunks: why, and which of your videos shows it?
cards.a2: One long point is hard to follow; points with sub-points keep attention. The glow-up video was split well, the carotenoid one wasn't.

cards.q: What's a leitmotif?
cards.a2: A recurring sound or music cue tied to one idea, place or character. Ryan Trahan's "da mountain".

cards.q: Big picture or details first, and why?
cards.a2: Big picture first. A caveman meeting a tiger asks "will it eat me?", not "how many teeth?". Why we debloat comes before potassium numbers.

cards.q: Contrast: where does it matter most?
cards.a2: When you open a curiosity gap or a B plot. If the viewer doesn't notice the gap, it was never opened.

cards.q: Rule 1 of YouTube?
cards.a2: If they don't click, they don't watch.

cards.q: What's a curiosity gap, and how do low-view titles usually fail it?
cards.a2:
A question the viewer can't answer and needs to.
Low-view titles either answer themselves or ask something everyone already knows.

cards.q: Make your content ___, your packaging ___.
cards.a2: Niche; broad.

cards.q: How many core elements in a thumbnail? Example?
cards.a2: 3 max. For example: you + text/arrow + one object.

cards.q: Title and thumbnail should ___, never ___.
cards.a2: Talk to each other (complement); never repeat each other.

cards.q: The glance test?
cards.a2: Show it for 2 seconds. Ask: what's it about, what stood out first, what do you remember? If they can't answer, it isn't clear.

cards.q: Why $295 instead of $300, and $45,000/month instead of $1M?
cards.a2: Odd, current numbers feel real and specific.

cards.q: Title words that lift views on face channels?
cards.a2: "for men / as a guy" 1.69×, tier list 1.40×, "I tried / I tested" 1.28×, age/teen 1.28×. Question marks: 0.86×.

cards.q: What matters in a face-channel thumbnail?
cards.a2: Your face, big, plus 1–3 words (face 1.24×, 1–3 words 1.12×). Before/after did NOT separate winners on face channels.

cards.q: Does thumbnail colour lift views?
cards.a2: No. Within a channel, colour, contrast and clutter stay within ±10%. Concept beats pixels.

cards.q: How should you A/B test thumbnails?
cards.a2: 3 macro-different concepts first, then micro tweaks (shirt, object, word) on the winner.

cards.q: Paddy's 5 hallmarks of a great idea?
cards.a2: Interesting to core, casual AND new viewers · easy to convey in title + thumbnail · novelty · combines proven formats · friends get excited when you mention it.

cards.q: The party question?
cards.a2: What are you bringing that the party doesn't already have? Jägermeister, not more Finlandia.

cards.q: Why does "___ Is Designed to Fail" work?
cards.a2: It makes viewers feel set up (paranoia + victimhood), and you become the truth-teller. "Your Skincare Routine Is Designed to Fail."

cards.q: Which title format was a 470× outlier?
cards.a2: "What [Authority] Won't Tell You (But I Will)".

cards.q: The insulin title: format and result?
cards.a2: "If You Don't Understand Insulin, You Don't Understand Fat Loss": 250K+ views on a channel averaging ~1K. Tie what they want to a hidden factor.

cards.q: Negativity framing: the Bezos CTR example?
cards.a2: "Dumb Things Jeff Bezos Wastes His Billions On" 3.13% CTR vs "How Billionaire Jeff Bezos Spends All His Money" 2.30%.

cards.q: Lists vs "how to" in Jake Thomas's tests?
cards.a2: Lists won 3 out of 3. "5 Tips To Make Your Videos Cinematic" 2.51% vs "How To Make Your Videos Look Cinematic" 1.90%.

cards.q: What should a thumbnail look like, per Paddy?
cards.a2: Like an action: a frame you could press play on. For education, show a process.

cards.q: When do you sketch the thumbnail?
cards.a2: Before filming, so you capture the shot you need.

cards.q: Why study billboards and movie posters?
cards.a2: They're made by people whose whole job is a one-second read. Steal formats from outside YouTube.

cards.q: Purple cow: what's the lesson and the catch?
cards.a2: Remarkable stands out. The catch: only while it's rare. If every cow is purple, nobody cares. Have your own angle, not a copied format.

cards.q: The 3 most important YouTube metrics?
cards.a2: CTR, average view duration, returning viewers.

cards.q: Healthy numbers right after an upload?
cards.a2: CTR over 5%, ~70% still watching at 30 s, and on a 12-min video over 50% average view duration.

cards.q: Returning viewers are low. What's the first question?
cards.a2: Am I targeting a different identity with every video? Build every video for one person who'd watch most of them.

cards.q: Your channel promise?
cards.a2: "I will help you become more attractive." Fans trust the promise, so they click whatever the packaging.

cards.q: Your common enemy, and the 3 contrasts with it?
cards.a2:
Blackpill / extreme looksmaxxing.
Mental health (they get depressed, you do the opposite), physical health (only safe methods), legitimacy (only proven methods).

cards.q: Airrack's community test for any idea?
cards.a2: Would ~80% of this video's viewers also watch your other videos? 50M empty views don't build a community.

cards.q: "Package every video for a stranger, but film it for ___."
cards.a2: …the 16-year-old who's been watching since the start.

cards.q: "Make it a show": how does it apply to you?
cards.a2: Series with a recurring cue, ideally back to back. N-day tests rated 1–10 each time, so viewers binge the series like one thing.

cards.q: Dan Mace's 3 tips?
cards.a2: Reframe the intro so people care (the shoes → education line), interested is interesting, repeat objects (a signature item).

cards.q: How to upload (your routine)?
cards.a2: Upload unlisted first so YouTube processes it. Post a community post as it goes public. Don't watch your fresh upload unless you watch to the end.

cards.q: How do you mention the Discord?
cards.a2: Naturally: "we've been talking about this in the Discord". Make videos that answer Discord questions. It shows a living community.

cards.q: Top 3 traits when hiring someone for the channel?
cards.a2: Coachability, real interest in the topic, wanting to go further with you.

cards.q: MrBeast's way of training a team member?
cards.a2: Spend a huge amount of time with them. They watch you do every detail for months and become like you, then train 3 others the same way.

cards.q: "Be where your competition isn't": your combination?
cards.a2: Attractiveness for young guys + cinematic + jokes. Plus your edges: being young and having an aesthetic body.

cards.q: What makes a cult-like audience (pick 4 of your 7)?
cards.a2: A common enemy, a very specific niche, giving the viewer ownership, being who he wants to be, being his bro, being funny, recurring jokes.

cards.q: Talk Like TED's 3 Ps of delivery?
cards.a2: Passion, Practice, Presence.

cards.q: What should your delivery sound like?
cards.a2: An exciting dinner conversation with a friend: more energy than real life, but a conversation, never reading.

cards.q: 4 gesture rules?
cards.a2: Hands free. Use gestures sparingly and naturally. Save the biggest for key moments. Keep them above the waist.

cards.q: Eager vs reserved nonverbal style?
cards.a2:
Eager: animated, broad open moves, leaning forward. It makes an offer more attractive.
Reserved: leaning back, small slow moves, slow speech.

cards.q: Power posing: what can you honestly say?
cards.a2: It may make you FEEL a bit more confident. The testosterone/cortisol claims failed to replicate (Ranehill 2015).

cards.q: 5 things to control in your voice?
cards.a2: Speed, volume, pauses, emphasis, pitch. Let the important lines breathe.

cards.q: Why must you believe every line you say?
cards.a2: If you don't, your body and voice show it. Viewers have watched thousands of videos and can spot it.

cards.q: Ali Abdaal's "unblocking": what is it?
cards.a2: Take the stone out of your shoe instead of running to dinner bleeding. Remove what blocks the task instead of forcing it with discipline.

cards.q: NICE goals?
cards.a2: Near-term, Input-based, Controllable, Energizing.

cards.q: The 4 questions before a task you might avoid?
cards.a2: A week passed and you haven't started: what are the 3 reasons? How can you reduce each? Who can help? What can you do right now?

cards.q: How can rewards kill motivation? The studies?
cards.a2: Kids who expected a reward for drawing drew less afterwards (Lepper 1973). Paid puzzle-solvers played less in their free time (Deci 1971). Love the process.

cards.q: What did the "I forgive myself" study find?
cards.a2: Students who forgave themselves for procrastinating procrastinated less before the next exam (Wohl 2010).

cards.q: The 10/10/10 question?
cards.a2: Will this matter in 10 minutes? In 10 weeks? In 10 years?

cards.q: Asking face to face vs by message?
cards.a2: In-person requests were about 34× more effective than email (Roghanizad & Bohns 2017).

cards.q: "Errors are the basis for neuroplasticity." So what do you do?
cards.a2: Make more errors, with feedback. A weak video is the heavy set that builds the good one.

cards.q: Your definition of growth?
cards.a2: Putting in effort, and putting it in the right place. Views don't decide whether you're doing well.

cards.q: The Swedish saying, and what to do with it?
cards.a2: Shared joy is double joy, shared sorrow is half sorrow. React with energy when someone tells you good news.

cards.q: The 5 whys: what's it for?
cards.a2: Before a new task, ask why 5 times. If it doesn't lead to something important long-term, it may be a waste of time.

cards.q: "What's the next step?": give an example.
cards.a2: Ask for the smallest physical step. Script avoided → open Notion. Gym avoided → put your shoes on.

cards.q: Bloat or fat: how do you tell?
cards.a2: Water changes within a day (puffier in the morning, slimmer at night). Fat takes weeks to months.

cards.q: Average sodium intake vs the WHO limit?
cards.a2: About 4,300 mg a day on average vs under 2,000 mg (5 g salt).

cards.q: Why does potassium help with bloat?
cards.a2: It makes the kidneys excrete more sodium. It helps your body get rid of the salt.

cards.q: Why do carbs add water weight?
cards.a2: Each gram of stored glycogen holds about 3 g of water, and insulin makes the kidneys hold on to sodium.

cards.q: Calf raises after meals (soleus push-up): what's proven?
cards.a2: They cut the blood-sugar spike by about half (Hamilton 2022). Not proven to debloat your face directly.

cards.q: Can you spot-reduce face fat?
cards.a2: No. Fat loss isn't local. A face slims through overall fat loss and less water retention.

cards.q: Jawline gum: what does the best evidence say?
cards.a2: Bite force goes up, but a 6-month RCT in young adults (Jung 2024, n=58) found no change in masseter size or jaw shape. The pump is temporary; heavy use risks TMJ pain.

cards.q: Mewing in adults?
cards.a2: No controlled evidence it reshapes bone.

cards.q: Veggie tan: what's the evidence?
cards.a2: More fruit & veg makes skin more golden within ~6 weeks, and it's rated healthier and more attractive. Carotenoid colour beat melanin (tan) colour in those studies (Whitehead 2012; Stephen 2011).

cards.q: First-line acne treatment you can put on your skin, and how long until it works?
cards.a2: A retinoid like adapalene. About 8–12 weeks. Expect some irritation; wear sunscreen.

cards.q: Blue-light glasses for sleep?
cards.a2: A Cochrane review (2023) found little or no effect. Lower brightness and screen time instead.

cards.q: Does sleep change how attractive you look?
cards.a2: Yes: sleep-deprived people were rated less attractive and more tired (Axelsson 2010; Sundelin 2017).

cards.q: Why do you look worse in selfies?
cards.a2: At about 30 cm the lens makes the nose look ~30% wider than at 1.5 m (Ward 2018). Hold the phone further away or zoom in.

cards.q: Why do you like your mirror face more than photos?
cards.a2: Mere exposure: you see your mirrored face every day, so the real (camera) version feels off (Mita 1977).

cards.q: What do r/LooksmaxingAdvice posters want most?
cards.a2: A verdict and a priority order: ~44% of posts are rate-me / "what should I fix?". The crowd's #1 fix: haircut, then beard, leaner, clothes.

cards.q: "Can I still grow?": how big is that question?
cards.a2: 16% of questions under the top height videos. Height how-to hits 2× on 56% of face-channel videos.

cards.q: Facial contrast research: the catch?
cards.a2: It's mostly studied on women's faces. In men, contrast is tied more to looking younger and healthier.

cards.q: Hunter eyes without surgery?
cards.a2: The shape is mostly bone and fat structure. You can reduce under-eye puffiness and groom brows, not change the shape.

cards.q: Ego depletion (willpower runs on glucose): true?
cards.a2: It failed a 23-lab replication (Hagger 2016). Don't say it on camera.

cards.q: Why are emotional moments remembered better?
cards.a2: The amygdala (in the temporal lobe, not the prefrontal cortex) and noradrenaline strengthen hippocampus memory. That's why a jaw-dropping moment sticks.

cards.q: What should you obsess over instead of analytics?
cards.a2: Good ideas. Spend far more time on the idea and the angle (the tier list changed your whole first video): write several versions with different angles and pick the best.

cards.q: Personal brand = ?
cards.a2: What you do + what you believe in + how they remember you. Be the example everywhere they find you, have a story, and keep what you say and do the same.

cards.q: MrBeast's question to ask yourself every day?
cards.a2: "Why don't you work more?" And always be a student: he called a far smaller creator for the chance of one spark.

cards.q: What is a "core", Southwest-style?
cards.a2: One simple question every decision can be checked against. Southwest: "does this help us be the cheapest airline?" Anyone can apply it without a script.

cards.q: Packaging, intro, editing and script should…
cards.a2: …all feel like they belong to the same video. And stick to the core idea, for the channel and the video.

cards.q: How do you make a video faster?
cards.a2: Set a self-imposed deadline ("the deadline is Monday"): realistic, but a bit hard.

cards.q: What's the real reward when you make a video?
cards.a2: Getting to make it. The effort makes you grow, and growth is the reward. Views and comments are a separate bonus.

teach.q: bro why is my face puffier in the morning than at night??
points: It's water, not fat: it can change in a day
Lying flat overnight lets fluid settle in the face; standing and moving during the day drains it
Salty, carby or boozy dinners make you hold more water by morning
Fixes: less salt at dinner, potassium foods, move after meals

teach.q: my cousin says if i chew jawline gum every day i'll get a chad jaw. true?
points: Bite force goes up
Best RCT (Jung 2024, young adults, 6 months): no change in masseter size or jaw shape
The 'pump' right after chewing is temporary
Heavy use can cause jaw (TMJ) pain or headaches
Jaw definition depends mostly on body fat

teach.q: is mewing gonna fix my jaw? i'm 18
points: No controlled evidence that mewing reshapes adult bone
Normal tongue posture is harmless, but don't expect a new jaw
Body fat, haircut, beard and posture change how your jaw looks much more
Avoid hard mewing / bone smashing: risk with no proven benefit

teach.q: i've tried like 5 face washes and my acne won't go away. what do i do
points: Face washes are rarely the fix
A retinoid like adapalene is first-line; benzoyl peroxide also helps
Give it 8–12 weeks and be consistent
Moisturise and wear sunscreen (retinoids irritate and sensitise)
See a dermatologist if it's severe or scarring

teach.q: why do i look so ugly in selfies but fine in the mirror
points: Close-up lens distortion: at ~30 cm the nose looks ~30% wider (Ward 2018)
Mirror familiarity: you're used to your flipped face (mere exposure)
Lighting and angle matter a lot
Fix: phone further away / 2× zoom, light in front of you, camera slightly above eye level

teach.q: can eating carrots actually change my skin colour lol
points: Yes: carotenoids from fruit & veg build up in skin
Visible golden tone in about 6 weeks
Rated healthier and more attractive in studies, even more than a tan
Variety of colourful fruit & veg, not only carrots
Only extreme amounts turn you orange

teach.q: what's the ONE thing i should fix first to look better?
points: Most common answer from 905K posts: a haircut that suits your face
Then: lower body fat (shows your jaw and face shape), clear skin
Ignore bone-structure hacks first
Fix the cheap, high-impact things in order

teach.q: does salt really make my face look fat?
points: More salt than usual → your body holds more water for a while
It often shows in the face first
Average intake ~4,300 mg vs the WHO limit of 2,000 mg
It's water, so it comes off in days, unlike fat
Potassium helps the body get rid of sodium

teach.q: should i sleep less so i have more time for gym and stuff?
points: Sleep-deprived people are rated less attractive and more tired-looking
Muscle recovery and training get worse
Less sleep raises hunger and makes fat loss harder
Keep 7–9 hours; it's the cheapest looks upgrade

teach.q: how do i get hunter eyes?
points: Eye shape is mostly bone, fat and genetics
No exercise or mewing has evidence for changing it
You CAN reduce puffiness and dark circles (sleep, salt) and groom your brows
Don't fall for surgery hype at 18

teach.q: am i still growing at 18?
points: Many guys stop around 16–18, some grow into their early 20s
Growth stops when growth plates close (an X-ray can show it)
Clues: grown in the last year? shoe size still changing? when did your dad stop?
Posture adds apparent height; stretching or supplements don't add height after plates close

teach.q: does face yoga slim your face?
points: You can't spot-reduce fat
The one small study (Alam 2018, middle-aged women) showed fuller cheeks, not slimmer
A face slims from overall fat loss and less water retention

teach.q: why can't our intro just start with 'hey guys welcome back'?
points: Viewers decide in seconds, and autoplay is muted
Result-first openings win (15% of winners vs 5%); greeting first loses (9% vs 22%)
The first seconds must confirm the click from the thumbnail
Greetings tell strangers the video is for old fans

teach.q: what even is a curiosity gap and how do i put one in an intro?
points: A question the viewer can't answer but wants to
Open it by ~0:30 (our viewers left at 0:22–0:37)
Example: '3 steps, and the third is the one nobody does'
Make it clear (contrast) and close it later in the video

teach.q: why do you care so much that the first 10 seconds match the thumbnail?
points: The viewer clicked for a promise and checks it immediately
A mismatch feels like clickbait → he leaves
Confirming the click is Paddy's rule 1
It protects trust, which the channel is built on

teach.q: why can't i put like 6 things in the thumbnail?
points: It's read in about a second on a phone
Max 3 core elements
On face channels: big face + 1–3 words wins
Use the glance test: 2 seconds, what's it about?

teach.q: why are you obsessed with returning viewers?
points: They show a real community, not random views
They come from serving one identity every time
Fans trust the channel promise and click whatever the packaging
Airrack: consistency compounds; empty views don't

teach.q: how do you know an idea is good before we script it?
points: Interesting to core, casual and new viewers
Easy to show in a title and thumbnail
Something new (novelty)
Uses a proven format
Friends get excited when you say it

teach.q: why do you keep asking 'does this move the story forward?' in the edit?
points: Viewers want new information
Repetition and setup lines make people leave
Faster isn't better, but wasted seconds are
Lower cognitive load: one clear thing at a time

teach.q: what's the point of a B plot?
points: The A plot is what the packaging promised
The B plot is the unexpected extra
Over-delivering is the opposite of clickbait
It turns viewers into fans who trust the next click

teach.q: why do you always call step 1 the most important?
points: The biggest drop-off is at the start
Framing step 1 as crucial hooks people there
Each later step gets framed as crucial in a new way
The best payoff still comes at the end (escalation)

teach.q: how do i make a boring stat actually interesting?
points: Compare it to something concrete (the popcorn example)
Make it about the viewer's daily life
Add emotion: surprise, disgust, relief
Show it visually instead of just saying the number

teach.q: why should we edit for emotion and not just make it look cool?
points: Edits should make the viewer feel something
Don't show off editing skills
If it's too fast or cluttered to understand, cut it
Music and sound follow the story; sound used sparingly

teach.q: why put personal stories in an educational video?
points: Stories hit emotion first, then logic
Brains sync during stories (brain-to-brain coupling)
Viewers want a human, which is why AI channels can't build community
Gives a hero to root for and builds trust

fix.bad: Hey guys, welcome back to my channel! Today we're gonna talk about debloating your face, which is something a lot of you have asked about. So let's get into it.
fix.task: Rewrite the first ~15 seconds. No greeting, show the result, open a loop.
rules: Show the result in the first seconds
Seamless bridge, no 'let's get into it'
fix.model: [Bloated vs debloated photo, same lighting] This is my face two days apart. Same guy, same body fat. The difference is water, and by the end of this video you'll know the 4 things that control it. One of them has nothing to do with food, and it's the first one.

fix.task: Rewrite the title so it has a curiosity gap and names the viewer.
